questions.question: What makes an interface a functional interface?
options: It has no methods at all
It has exactly one abstract method
questions.explanation: One abstract method is the rule. Default and static methods are allowed and do not count.

questions.question: What does this print? Function<Integer, Integer> twice = x -> x * 2; System.out.println(twice.apply(21));
questions.explanation: apply runs the lambda body with x = 21, and the single expression 21 * 2 is returned automatically.

questions.question: int total = 0; scores.forEach(r -> total += r); Why does this not compile?
options: r must have a declared type
total is changed inside the lambda, so it is not effectively final
questions.explanation: Captured locals must be effectively final. Use scores.stream().mapToInt(r -> r).sum() to get the total instead.

questions.question: What does this print? Predicate<String> longName = s -> s.length() > 4; System.out.println(longName.test("Dhoni") + " " + longName.negate().test("Dhoni"));
questions.explanation: Dhoni has 5 letters, so test returns true. negate() flips the rule, so the second call returns false.

questions.question: Which built-in functional interface takes no input and returns a value?
questions.explanation: Supplier<T> has T get(). Consumer takes input and returns nothing, Predicate returns boolean, Function converts.

questions.question: Why does Object o = () -> "six"; fail to compile?
options: Object is not a functional interface, so the lambda has no target method
The parentheses must contain a parameter
A lambda needs braces around its body
questions.explanation: A lambda needs a functional interface as its target type. Assign it to something like Supplier<String> instead.

questions.question: What does this print? BiFunction<Integer, Integer, Integer> sr = (r, b) -> r * 100 / b; System.out.println(sr.apply(30, 20));
questions.explanation: 30 * 100 is 3000, and integer division by 20 gives 150.

questions.question: Inside a lambda written in an instance method, what does the keyword this refer to?
options: The enclosing object whose method contains the lambda
It is not allowed inside a lambda
questions.explanation: A lambda does not create its own this. In an anonymous class, by contrast, this means the anonymous object.

questions.question: What does this print? Runnable r = () -> System.out.print("A"); System.out.print("B"); r.run();
questions.explanation: Creating the lambda does not run it. B prints first, and A prints only when r.run() is called.

questions.question: What does the @FunctionalInterface annotation do?
options: It makes the interface run faster
It is required before any lambda can be used
It makes the compiler check that the interface has exactly one abstract method
It turns every method into a default method
questions.explanation: The annotation is optional. It is a safety net that fails compilation if someone adds a second abstract method.
